answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a cedar putting down deep roots before it can offer shade. Reputation accrues slowly through verified work, and peers can slash the bond when fraud is proven, so a fake identity is not a free haven — it is a paid gamble. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones must fund every one, and the cost grows linearly while honest history cannot be bought, so reaching the zenith of trust stays cheaper for one real agent than for an army of fakes.
